summary: Request timeouts for long-context prompts and large max_tokens causing streaming disconnects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports requests entering timeouts and streaming disconnects when sending long-context prompts (20k+ tokens) or setting very large max_tokens (>= 16384). Instances appear to stall or return HTTP 504 / grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED after ~60s.

Impact:
- Customer (Acme Health, dedicated) experiencing failed completion requests for batch inference pipelines and interactive assistant flows.
- Errors cause user-facing failures and retries, increasing cost and latency.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool for Acme Health in us-east-1, running redwood-verified-13b-v2 and a quantized vicuna variant.
- Traffic via API Gateway -> Streaming proxy -> Serving runtime.

Steps to reproduce:
1) POST /v1/completions with model redwood-verified-13b-v2 in prod us-east.
2) Provide a context payload with ~22k tokens (long doc) and max_tokens set to 16384.
3) Enable streaming=true and client-side streaming consumer.
4) Observe request stalls and eventually returns 504 or stream closes with grpc status=DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.

Observed behavior:
- Streaming disconnects at ~60s.
- Server logs show repeated kernel stalls and high CPU on host; KV cache grows rapidly.
- Autoscaler did not spawn additional nodes before timeouts.

Expected behavior:
- Platform should either stream partial output before deadline or fail fast with clear error explaining token limits. Autoscaler should react to sustained CPU/KV pressure for dedicated pools.
steps_to_reproduce: Include a long prompt ~22k tokens and set max_tokens=16384
Set streaming=true and consume stream client-side
Observe for ~60s for timeout or disconnect
logs: [2026-02-25T14:04:27Z] serving-runtime: error: kernel stall detected, trace=/srv/logs/trace-9832.log
[2026-02-25T14:04:30Z] autoscaler: no scale event triggered for pool=dedicated-acme despite high CPU (threshold 85%)
comments: Customer (Acme Health) - 2026-02-25 14:12 UTC: We see a high rate of 504s on long documents. This blocks our intake pipeline. Any ETA?
Sofia Patel (Support) - 2026-02-25 14:20 UTC: Filed ticket and escalated to SRE. Asking for request/trace ids and recent logs (provided).

Liam Chen (SRE) - 2026-02-25 15:05 UTC: Reproduced locally with reduced token sets. Initial hypothesis: KV cache growth + contiguous memory allocation triggers kernel path that blocks streaming flushes. Collecting perf traces.

Ava Martinez (Infra) - 2026-02-25 17:30 UTC: Noted autoscaler config had aggressive cooldown; will create a temporary override to lower cooldown and allow one immediate scale-up for dedicated-acme pool.
Sofia Patel (Support) - 2026-02-26 09:02 UTC: Provided customer workaround: reduce max_tokens to <= 2048 or split context into chunks and stream successive calls. Customer testing now.
Customer (Acme Health) - 2026-02-26 10:10 UTC: Workaround reduced failures, but performance impact is unacceptable for some flows. Requesting permanent fix timeline.
Liam Chen (SRE) - 2026-02-27 08:45 UTC: Added a mitigation: enable early partial-flush for streaming on affected models and lowered autoscaler cooldown for the dedicated pool. Monitoring for 24h.
investigation_notes: Perf traces show extended memcpy and GPU kernel queuing when KV cache exceeds ~900MB for 13b models with long sequence lengths.
Serving runtime path responsible for checkpointing KV and streaming flush runs on main thread; this can be preempted by heavy attention kernel scheduling.
Autoscaler did not trigger due to 10min cooldown and insufficient sustained signal in the 60s window — consider changing scale triggers to include backlog/queue depth.
No indications of network packet drops between proxy and serving hosts; issue appears compute-bound.
Reproduced on redwood-verified-13b-v2; lower-precision quantized variants degrade similarly but have marginally lower memory growth.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer (reduce max_tokens <=2048, chunk context). Infrastructure mitigation deployed: lowered autoscaler cooldown for dedicated-acme pool and enabled early partial-flush for streaming on affected model variants. Follow-ups: (1) create a platform limit/guardrail to reject or warn on requests >12k combined tokens for 13b-class models, (2) refactor KV flush path to not block streaming thread, (3) add autoscaler metric for serving queue depth. Owner: Liam Chen. Target ETA for code fix: 2026-03-10.
